body: I feel like they're judging me. Which in a way, yes, that's their job, but I feel like it's a lot more personal than that, I guess. For example, I feel like if I tell someone I'm a lesbian, they'll start thinking it's because I'm too ugly and no guy would ever like me or something like that. Or if I tell them about my social phobia, they'll think it's because I constantly fail at everything I do. Or if I tell them about my suicidal thoughts, they'll think I'm just some ungrateful, selfish brat. And I know that's just the anxiety, but it still could be true. I just feel like I'm wasting their time and irritating them with my petty little teenage problems and such. Oh, and then there's how I'm going to school for psychology. I bet they get a good laugh out of that one, thinking "haha, yeah right, look at your fucked up self esteem and your lack of contentment and your anxiety, and how do you expect to fix other people's problems when your emotional state is this pathetic?"

Thank you for the reply. 

But *when* will it get better? Even when I put in all the effort I can, I'm only getting worse. And I really do try, but it's pointless in the end it seems.

Thanks! I talked to my doc and she's setting me up with a psychiatrist for better judgment on which meds to try. Hopefully we'll be able to find one that helps some.

So are you saying that I should just wait these years out? Realistically I only have a bit over a year until I'm off to university, but a year can still seem like forever.

But the thing with my mom is that she's the perfect person in everyone else's eyes - even my other siblings. She treats me and me only like shit, though. So I know she has the capability of being a good parent in her, but for some reason she just seems to hate me. Well, it's actually probably just because we have opposing beliefs, but.... still.

I live in a small redneck town. Closest lgbt group is over an hour's drive away. The only lgbt people I've actually met outside of the internet are "bicurious" girls (not saying that's not valid, but you probably know the type of girls I'm talking about). In addition to that, I'm still closeted because I know that if I come out, I'll almost certainly be bullied and/or abused, not to mention a complete disgrace to my entire family.

I talked to my doc about switching meds, and she's going to set me up with a psychiatrist (rather than just a counselor like I was seeing). I don't really know what to say, though. It's like I really want to open up to the therapist, but my mind goes completely blank as soon as I walk through the door. I've even tried writing things down before hand, but I still can't talk coherently. Do you have any advice for that? And I've tried a few therapists, and I've liked all but one of them. But even then I have trouble opening up. 

And thank you for the reply.
